beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: OpenDSU asks what must travel with data for it to remain controllable and verifiable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book explains a conceptual framework, rather than documenting one frozen software release.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central relationships connect protected content, authority, reconstructable structure, and verifiable history.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A cryptographic commitment can establish integrity without proving the truth of the content.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain distinctions for evaluating digital trust without asking one mechanism to guarantee everything.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A copied file can retain its content while losing its history or policy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A Data Sharing Unit instead gives related information an accountable logical boundary.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Protected bricks and a protected map support reconstruction of the object's contents.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Compact anchoring evidence records continuity without placing the confidential contents on a shared ledger.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book explains why those relationships matter beyond any particular storage implementation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading, modification, and verification need not expose the same powers or information.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book distinguishes capability, provenance, validation, and the context where authority is exercised.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Each mechanism answers a limited question about the digital object.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A valid history can still contain false claims or reflect an unacceptable process.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those limits make the framework an argument about composed trust, rather than magical cryptography.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the verification gap before entering the technical vocabulary.
